reason: The development environment signals a fibroblast route, matching the goal of directing the stem-cell population toward connective-tissue work.
expectation: The signals will guide some cells toward becoming fibroblasts.

effect: The signals directed a subset toward fibroblasts and activated a collagen gene, producing messenger RNA for the next stage.
reaction: The link from an external signal to gene activity is useful, though the mesoderm precursor is not explained.
reason: The collagen messenger RNA is headed to ribosomes, where amino acids can be assembled into protein.

choice.combine: Developing fibroblasts with collagen messenger RNA

expectation: The fibroblasts will use the amino acids to make a collagen precursor.

effect: The fibroblasts now produce procollagen in the ER and Golgi; the new goal is to use secreted protein outside the cells.
reaction: The RNA-to-protein picture makes the next stage clear.
reason: The secretory vesicles are described as carrying procollagen from the Golgi and fusing with the cell membrane.
expectation: The vesicles will release procollagen outside the fibroblasts.

effect: Procollagen is now outside the fibroblasts, ready for extracellular processing.
reaction: The vesicle-fusion sequence clearly connects protein production to secretion.
reason: The processing enzymes are described as clipping secreted procollagen and cross-linking collagen molecules.
expectation: The enzymes will process the procollagen into organized collagen fibers.

effect: The procollagen has become cross-linked collagen fibers that resist tension; the hydrated proteoglycans remain available to build extracellular material.
reaction: The tension arrows make the fibers' structural role clear.
reason: The proteoglycan picture shows a water-rich gel with space for collagen fibers, matching the extracellular-material goal.
expectation: The fibers and hydrated gel will form extracellular matrix.

effect: The fibers and hydrated gel formed extracellular matrix, completing the goal while keeping the fibroblasts distinct from the material around them.
reaction: The cell-versus-matrix inset makes that distinction clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the signal through collagen gene activity, protein production and secretion was most worthwhile: it connects gene expression to a material cells put outside themselves.

leastWorthwhile.text: The mesoderm precursor appeared in the development sequence without an explanation, making that transition harder to follow.

surprise.text: The final illustration plan explicitly distinguishes fibroblasts from the matrix they make, rather than implying the cells become the matrix.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the item descriptions gave a clear purpose for each combination.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how this cell-to-matrix construction connects to larger tissues, although the mostly predictable combinations offered few difficult decisions.
